The Cipher Lab

Interactive tools built on Trithemius’s actual tables — encode and decode messages through the Polygraphia’s verbal-substitution ciphers, explore the tabula recta, and consult the Steganographia’s catalogue of spirits.

Encoder / Decoder Tabula Recta Side-by-side Comparison Numerical Letters Spirit Index

Encoder & Decoder

Type a message and watch it become a pious Latin sentence through the Ave Maria cipher — each plaintext letter is replaced by a real word from the Polygraphia’s substitution columns, rotating by position.

↓

Tabula Recta

The 24×24 alphabet-rotation grid — the polyalphabetic table that prefigures the Vigenère cipher. Click a row and column to highlight the cipher letter.

Side-by-side Comparison

One plaintext, encoded four ways — to see why Trithemius escalated the complexity across his books.

Numerical Letters

Trithemius’s positional letter-codes for numbers (units a–i, tens k–r, hundreds, and w-suffixed magnitudes).

Some codes collide in the OCR’d source (e.g. cw, bw); ambiguous results are flagged.

Spirit Index — Steganographia

The sixteen cardinal princes of the winds, from the Table of Direction.
